title: Becoming a referee, and your referee profile
description: You cannot make yourself a referee. A tournament organiser adds you, and Scoryboard then gives your profile a referee side.
body:
You cannot make yourself a referee. Only a tournament organiser can, by adding you to one of their tournaments. Scoryboard then gives your profile a referee side, with its own bio and its own statistics.

Before you start

You need a Scoryboard account, and an organiser who is running a tournament. There is no referee sign-up. Nothing you can reach in your own account turns you into a referee.

How you become a referee

  1. Tell the organiser the email address your Scoryboard account uses.
  2. Ask them to add you as a referee on their tournament. On their side that is Participants, then Referees, then Add Referee. They fill in your name and that email address.

  3. Wait. Nothing arrives. Scoryboard sends no notification and no email when somebody adds you as a referee. Check your profile instead.

The email address has to match your account exactly. An address that belongs to nobody still works for the organiser: Scoryboard makes a referee record for that name. Nobody can sign in to it, and you get nothing.

Your referee profile

  1. Open your own profile. A blue switch has appeared at the top right, and it is set to Referee.

  2. Select Football on the switch to see your player profile again. Your two profiles hold different bios, different statistics and different match lists.

Your profile opens on the referee side from now on, because being added as a referee makes Referee your default profile. You can change that under Select your default profile in Profile settings.

Add your referee bio

Your referee bio is separate from your player bio. Readers see it when your profile is on the referee side.

  1. Select your name at the top of the sidebar. The block opens and shows how many profile fields are still empty.

  2. Select Complete your profile. Scoryboard takes you to Profile settings and jumps to the first field you have not filled in.
  3. Find Referee Bio under My Bio. It sits under your player bio and only referees have it.

  4. Write your bio. You get 150 characters over five lines, and the counter under the box shows what you have used.

  5. Select Save Changes. Your bio now shows on the referee side of your profile, above your referee statistics.

What your referee statistics count

MATCHES is the only tile that moves for a referee. It counts the matches you have been the referee on.

The card and goal tiles are your own playing figures. A referee is not in the line-up she officiates, so they stay at zero unless you also play.

TOTAL FOULS is always 0. Scoryboard does not record fouls for a referee, and the tile has nothing behind it.

AVERAGE RATING is what players have rated you after matches. See Rating a match, player, team or referee.

If it does not work

  • Your profile has no Referee switch. Nobody has added you yet, or they used a different email address. Ask the organiser which address they typed.
  • You are waiting for an invitation. There is not one. Being added as a referee happens without your involvement and without a message. Open your profile to check.
  • There is no Referee Bio box in Profile settings. The box only appears once you are a referee. See the first point.
  • Your bio disappeared after you changed your photo. Save your photo first and your bio last. Saving a new photo on its own clears your bio. See Profile settings - what you can change.
  • You want to stop being a referee. Ask the organiser to remove you from the tournament. There is no control for this in your own account.
